bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8; Crash State: sdb_free / ns_free / sdb_ns_free; Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: In radare2's ART bin plugin, a 4-byte input equal to `art\n` is enough to select `bin_art`. `load_buffer()` allocates an `Sdb` object for ART metadata, stores it as the `info` namespace under the binfile Sdb, and `r_bin_object_set_items()` then moves that same pointer into `RBinObject::kv` via `get_sdb()`. The plugin `destroy()` callback still calls `sdb_free(obj->kv)`, even though ownership has already moved to `RBinObject`. `object_delete_items()` later calls `sdb_free(o->kv)` on the same shared `Sdb *`, freeing it while the binfile `info` namespace still retains the raw pointer. During recursive namespace teardown, `ns_free()` passes that stale pointer back into `sdb_free()`, which reads freed `Sdb` fields and triggers the ASan heap-use-after-free.

source.description: Reads the first four attacker-controlled bytes into `tmp`; these bytes are the dispatch key that decides whether the ART plugin path, and its vulnerable teardown logic, will be used.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is exactly 4 bytes `61 72 74 0a` (`art\n`), passed to `r_bin_get_binplugin_by_bytes()` and then to `bin_art::check_bytes()` / `check_buffer()`.
source.note: For the witness, the entire buffer is copied into `tmp` and the next line compares it against `"art\n"`.

sink.description: The stale `Sdb *` retained in the `info` namespace is passed back into `sdb_free()` after the object has already been freed, so `sdb_free` reads freed `Sdb` fields.
sink.note: ASan reports a heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at this conditional while evaluating the freed `Sdb` object.

root_cause.description: The ART plugin destroy callback still releases `obj->kv` even though `r_bin_object_set_items()` has already moved the same `Sdb *` into `RBinObject::kv` and the binfile `info` namespace still references it. This premature extra release is the ownership bug fixed by the patch.
root_cause.note: The fix deletes this line; after `get_sdb()` the `Sdb *` is owned by `RBinObject`, not by the plugin-private `ArtObj`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzzer writes the raw attacker-controlled bytes into the memory-backed file that the later `oba 0` / `ia` command sequence opens and probes as a binary.
tainted_value_origin.note: The staged witness is exactly 4 bytes long and contains only `art\n`.

parser_admitted.description: For the 4-byte PoC, this ART magic check returns true, so `r_bin_get_binplugin_by_bytes()` selects the ART plugin and the vulnerable load/teardown path executes.

coarse_trace.summary: Consumes the probed bytes and accepts the 4-byte witness as an ART file because it starts with `art\n`, selecting the ART bin plugin.
Allocates `ao->kv` for ART metadata, ignores the short-input failure from `art_header_load()`, and stores the same `Sdb *` in the binfile `info` namespace.
Calls the plugin `get_sdb()` hook and assigns the returned `ao->kv` pointer to `RBinObject::kv`, so the plugin object, the bin object, and the namespace all alias the same `Sdb` allocation.
During binfile teardown, the plugin destroy callback still calls `sdb_free(obj->kv)` even though ownership has already moved to `RBinObject`.
The later `sdb_free(o->kv)` in `object_delete_items()` releases the same `Sdb *` again and frees it while the `info` namespace still keeps the raw pointer.
Recursive namespace cleanup later walks the stale `info` namespace entry and passes its freed `Sdb *` back into `sdb_free()`, producing the ASan heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Copies the first four attacker-controlled bytes from the probed buffer into `tmp`. For the staged witness, `tmp` becomes the entire 4-byte file: `art\n`.

Evaluates true for the witness, so the plugin probe accepts the input as ART and `r_bin_get_binplugin_by_bytes()` selects `bin_art`. This control decision is the only input-dependent gate needed for the bug path.
After the ART plugin is selected, `load_buffer()` allocates the `Sdb` object that will hold ART metadata and later become the freed object reported by ASan.

Stores the newly allocated `ao->kv` under the binfile `info` namespace and increments its Sdb reference count. The 4-byte PoC still reaches this step because `load_buffer()` ignores the false return from `art_header_load()` on short input and returns `ao` anyway.

fine_trace.code: if (cp->get_sdb) { Sdb* new_kv = cp->get_sdb (binfile); if (new_kv != o->kv) { sdb_free (o->kv); } o->kv = new_kv; }
fine_trace.note: The plugin `get_sdb()` hook returns `ao->kv`, and `r_bin_object_set_items()` assigns that same pointer to `o->kv` after freeing the old placeholder `o->kv`. From this point, `obj->kv`, `o->kv`, and the namespace entry created in step 4 all alias the same `Sdb *`.

The plugin destroy callback releases the shared `Sdb *` even though ownership has already moved to `o->kv` and the `info` namespace still points to it. Because the namespace still holds a reference, this call does not free the object yet; it only drops the refcount one step early.

Teardown later releases the same aliased `Sdb *` through `RBinObject::kv`. Because step 6 already consumed the extra owner, this second release drops the shared object to zero references and frees it, while the `info` namespace entry from step 4 still stores the raw pointer because no `sdb_ns_unset()` removes it.

Later, recursive namespace teardown reaches the stale `info` namespace entry and loads its stored pointer into `ns->sdb`. The Stage 01 stack shows this happens during nested `ns_free` / `sdb_ns_free` calls from `r_core_fini()`.

Called with the freed pointer from step 8, `sdb_free()` dereferences the dead `Sdb` object while checking `s->ht` and `s->refs`. ASan reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at this line.

format.name: ART
format.contract: A 4-byte file whose entire contents are exactly `61 72 74 0a` (`art\n`). These bytes make `bin_art::check_buffer()` return true and select the ART plugin. No additional ART structure is required for this bug path because `load_buffer()` still allocates `ao->kv`, inserts it into the `info` namespace, and returns success even when `art_header_load()` fails on the short input.
